title: GPU CI Release Safety Lab and SLO Simulator
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Overview

This document describes the GPU CI Release Safety Lab: a reproducible, self-serve environment and simulation harness used by the infra team to validate GPU workload releases against SLOs, cost budgets, and multi-tenant fairness constraints before any wide canary or production rollout. The Safety Lab ties CI pipelines, Terraform/IaC templates, and a lightweight SLO simulator to provide deterministic pass/fail decisions that are enforced by the release gatekeeper.

Goals

- Provide an automated, low-cost simulation that predicts 95th and 99th percentile token latency impact for a proposed runtime change or kernel rollout.
- Surface cost delta estimates (per 1M tokens) and burst credit impact of a change.
- Enforce fairness checks (no single tenant > 40% additional tail latency in simulated mixed workloads).
- Produce deterministic artifacts (simulation report, telemetry diffs, Terraform plan assertions) that CI gates use to block merges.

Who should use this

- GPU runtime engineers validating kernel or scheduler changes.
- CI/CD owners and release engineers creating canary gating logic.
- SREs investigating latency regressions and wanting reproducible repros.

High-level architecture

1. CI job triggers Safety Lab: Buildkite job "gpu-safety-lab" runs unit+integration tests and then spins an ephemeral lab via Terraform.
2. Terraform brings up a small hetero pool (1-2 GPU nodes: mixed A100/RTX) in a dedicated sandbox account with scoped NAT and egress.
3. The harness deploys the proposed runtime artifact (docker image tag) and a controlled synthetic workload generator.
4. The SLO simulator runs the workload trace against both baseline and candidate artifacts to produce delta metrics.
5. CI collects the report, runs policy checks (thresholds, cost budget), and either passes the gate or requires a manual canary.

Key service names and components

- buildkite pipeline: pipelines/gpu-safety-lab-main
- terraform modules: tf-modules/ephemeral-gpu-lab and tf-modules/egress-fence
- lab harness: infra/safety-lab/runner (python)
- workload generator: tools/gpu-replay (replays recorded token-by-token traces)
- simulator: slo-sim v0.9 (sidecar service that consumes traces)
- artifacts registry: gcr.redwood-internal.com/redwood/runtime

Preflight checklist (CI in-job)

1. Verify artifact signature: cosign verify --key ksvc://release-keys $IMAGE
2. Run quick static assertions: python infra/safety-lab/validate_release.py --checks kernel-compat,quantization-profile
3. Run terraform plan with var overrides: terraform plan -var-file=ci/lab.auto.tfvars
4. Ensure cost budget token available: call cost-service /v1/budget/check?account=sandbox

Terraform pattern and example vars (table)

The lab uses a slim Terraform pattern to avoid long provisioning times. The important vars are documented below. Create tfvars for each CI run and attach to the Buildkite job.

| variable | description | example | required |
|----------|-------------|---------|----------|
| region | cloud region for ephemeral nodes | us-west-2 | yes |
| gpu_profile | node flavor set (hetero string) | ["A100:1","RTX8000:1"] | yes |
| egress_policy | egress fencing profile (strict/relaxed) | strict | yes |
| max_hours | auto-destroy after X hours | 2 | yes |
| billing_tag | cost center tag for chargeback | ci-safety-lab | yes |

Sample tfvars (ci/lab.auto.tfvars):

region = "us-west-2"
gpu_profile = ["A100:1", "RTX8000:1"]
egress_policy = "strict"
max_hours = 2
billing_tag = "ci-safety-lab"

SLOs and thresholds enforced by the harness

- 95th percentile token latency delta (candidate vs baseline): must be <= +8%
- 99th percentile token latency delta: must be <= +15%
- Token throughput regression: no more than 6% lower for same batch mix
- Fairness check: per-tenant tail latency increase must be < 40% (absolute)
- Cost estimate delta: per-1M-token cost must be <= +20% or flag a manual review

Failure modes and policy decisions

- If SLO simulator reports any threshold breach, the pipeline marks the run as "safety-failed" and attaches a generated report.
- Safety-failed → Automatic rollback of Terraform resources (destroy) + artifact quarantine + JIRA ticket created to releases board.
- If cost delta > 20% but SLOs pass, gate returns "requires-cost-review"; release engineers must complete a documented exception.

Detailed CI job steps (numbered)

1. Checkout and build runtime image (CI credentials limited to sandbox registry).
2. cosign verify and sign-off step using signer vault.
3. terraform init && terraform apply -auto-approve -var-file=ci/lab.auto.tfvars
4. wait-for-health-check script: infra/safety-lab/wait_health.sh $LAB_ENDPOINT --timeout 300s
5. deploy candidate image and baseline image side-by-side using router "lab-router" so generator can fanout traces independently.
6. run workload replay: python tools/gpu-replay/replay.py --trace traces/latency-sensitive-2025.json --target candidate
7. run slo-sim: python infra/safety-lab/slo_sim.py --baseline baseline:tag --candidate candidate:tag --workload traces/latency-sensitive-2025.json --output report.json
8. policy-check script parses report.json and exits non-zero if any assert fails.
9. terraform destroy -auto-approve (always run in a finally block to ensure cleanup).
10. artifact publish: store report.json in artifacts-bucket with lifecycle TTL 90 days; notify #infra-ci with summary.

Observability and telemetry deltas captured

- metrics collected: token.latency.p50/p95/p99, token.throughput, gpu.utilization, kernel-calls-per-token, kv-cache-hit-rate
- logs: runtime stdout/stderr, kernel debug traces (sampled), dmesg snapshots if OOM observed
- traces: opentelemetry spans with service_name=runtime-lab and an extra attribute candidate=true/false

Sample snafu: OOM spike during replay

1. CI job should surface: "oom: detected on node resource-1 during pass-2" in report.json
2. Auto-collect core shim: kubectl -n lab logs --selector app=runtime --tail=500 > oom.log
3. Run replay with --replay-window 10s to collect mini-traces to reproduce locally.
4. Tag and quarantine image; start a debug run with larger ephemeral node (A100:2) and kernel debug flags enabled.

Cost model snapshotting

The harness estimates cost via a compact model that maps GPU hours, egress, and per-token amortized amortization cost (image size, memory pressure impacts). The CI job records: estimated_cost_per_1M_tokens (USD) and an estimation breakdown. Example output snippet in report.json: 

{
  "baseline_cost_per_1M": "$110",
  "candidate_cost_per_1M": "$123",
  "egress_delta": "+$3",
  "gpu_hour_delta": "+0.08"
}

Security and account isolation

- Sandbox accounts are per-branch ephemeral accounts with least privilege service accounts provisioned by tf-modules/ephemeral-gpu-lab.
- Egress is fenced using a scoped NAT and egress-proxy that prevents access to internal data stores.
- All secrets are provided via transient Vault leases; keys are revoked on teardown.

Oncall / Runbook for failed safety-lab runs (short)

1. Triage summary posted to #oncall-infra automatically with run id, claim link, and short summary.
2. If terraform apply failed: collect terraform logs (CI artifact), inspect cloud provider error codes. If quota-related, escalate to cloud-accounts channel with request id and cost center.
3. If slo_sim reports tail latency regression: attach report, run a targeted local replay with --sample-seed from the report.
4. If repeated failures for same change across 3 runs: open incident and assign to runtime-oncall, mark severity P2.

Maintenance and operational notes

- Keep lab Terraform module versions locked (we recommend a major upgrade cadence aligned to monthly infra maintenance windows).
- Heavy traces should be downsampled to <1M tokens for CI runs; full 5M traces reserved for nightly long-runs.
- Lifetime of lab resources default to 2 hours; set max_hours=4 only for manual debug runs.

Debugging tips and utilities

- Reproduce locally: python infra/safety-lab/local_repro.py --image candidate:tag --trace traces/latency-sensitive-2025.json --nodes 1
- Quick kernel telemetry extractor: tools/kernel-telemetry/extract.sh --pid $PID --out kernel.tsv
- Use the SLO-sim interactive report: open https://observability.redwood.internal/slo-sim/reports/$RUN_ID (requires SSO)

Acceptance criteria for adding a new workload trace to the lab catalog

1. Workload must include a labeled tenant mix with at least 3 distinct tenant ids.
2. Trace must be annotated with token-level timestamps, batch sizes, and request metadata.
3. Size limit: nightly traces up to 5M tokens; CI traces must be <= 1M tokens.
4. A short README with origin, business owner, and a baseline pass report must be attached.

Related docs and references

- See tf-modules/ephemeral-gpu-lab README for module inputs and outputs.
- See infra/safety-lab/README.md for local runner options and env var matrix.
- Related runbook: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-latency-regression-investigation-playbook.json

Appendix: example Buildkite snippet (yaml)

steps:
  - label: "gpu-safety-lab"
    command:
      - scripts/ci/build-and-publish.sh
      - scripts/ci/run-safety-lab.sh --tfvars ci/lab.auto.tfvars
    env:
      LAB_TTL: 7200
      TF_VAR_billing_tag: ci-safety-lab
    agents:
      queue: gpu-ci

End of document
